chapter: Europe 1933, New York Cotton Club, Hodges group
title: The 1933 European trip and playing for the Prince of Wales
summary: The trip was hectic with theaters and private parties for the Prince of Wales and Lord Beaverbrook; Brown was seasick on the boat.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: It sounds good. Tell me about the trip to Europe.
Well there were many of them. Which ones you mean?

Oh, well that was a hectic trip because we were pioneering, according to certain people. And it entailed quite a few little incidents. We would play in a theater and then play a dance -- go to play a dance or a party -- mostly a party -- private party.
We played for a party at the Prince of Wales -- for the Prince of Wales. Oh many parties. Played Lord Beaverbrook's house and places like that.
Barry Ulanov says (Inaudible) the Prince of Wales sat in with the band once.
No. He -- not that I know of. But he was at this party all night. And you know you don't leave until the prince leaves. And so they had a very nice time and that's all I remember, I think.
And you went over -- you sailed.
We went on boat -- yeah, went by boat. Which I spent most of my time laying flat on my back to keep from getting sick so I didn't see much of the trip.
The band wasn't playing on the boat like they did in subsequent trips.

Not the first time -- I don't know -- I can't remember. We may have played a couple of numbers for the last night. Yeah, they usually -- everybody does something. The entertainers do something that last night you know before you dock.

I think we did play.
